jobs.title: Senior Cyber Operations Analyst (TS Cleared)
jobs.description:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

MITRE is seeking an experienced Senior Cyber Analyst who will lead high-visibility/high-impact efforts that provide significant contributions to the safety and security of the United States. The position will work closely with sponsor staff and regularly engage with senior leaders to understand their priorities and shape work. Major focus areas include criminal network analysis and disruption, digital marketplaces, and transnational criminal organizations and associated activities. Additional areas of responsibility include cybercrime investigation improvement, cyber-mission systems engineering and guidance, system-of-system engineering, data engineering and analysis, experimentation, communications, and acquisition.

Roles & Responsibilities:

In this role, the selected candidate will provide strategic and operational leadership as a trusted advisor to senior leaders within the sponsor’s organization in the areas of analysis and tradecraft in the fight against crime. Further, the selected candidate will contribute to efforts to:

Conduct Threat Intelligence Analysis: Perform proactive research and analysis of current and emerging cyber threats, with an emphasis on understanding threat actor motivations, tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
Perform Crypto tracing and Blockchain Analysis: Analyze blockchain transactions to trace cryptocurrency movements associated with malicious activities, collaborating with law enforcement and internal teams to identify potential threat actors.
Provide Attribution Analysis: Perform deep-dive analysis to identify threat actors, correlate various data sources, and leverage cyber threat intelligence databases to establish attribution.
Monitor and Analyze Dark Web Activities: Regularly assess and monitor Dark Web forums, marketplaces, and communication channels to gather intelligence on cybercriminals and their operations.
Develop Threat Reports and Briefings: Prepare comprehensive intelligence reports, briefings, and presentations that translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable insights for stakeholders.
Collaborate Cross-functionally: Work with other analysts, engineers, and threat intelligence teams to integrate findings, contribute to investigations, and enhance overall security posture.
Identify and Communicate Threat Trends: Proactively identify trends, vulnerabilities, and indicators of compromise (IoCs) to provide timely intelligence and risk assessments.
Drive Problem-solving Initiatives: Seek out difficult problems within the cyber threat landscape and address them innovatively. Serve as a go-to expert when team members and stakeholders face challenging cybersecurity issues.

Basic Qualifications:

Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 3 years and a Master’s degree; or a PhD with relevant experience who can immediately contribute at this job step; or equivalent combination of related education and work experience.
3-5 years of experience in cyber threat intelligence, crypto tracing, digital forensics, or a related field.
Relevant certifications (e.g., CEH, GCTI, GIAC) are a plus.
Relevant prior military and/or law enforcement experience can be accepted in place of formal education and/or experience requirements.
Analytical Skills: Demonstrated ability to analyze complex datasets and draw meaningful insights. Ability to think critically, recognize patterns, and correlate disparate data points.
Communication Skills: Strong written and verbal communication skills with experience in creating analytical reports, summaries, and visual presentations tailored to different audiences.
Self-motivation: Must be a self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced environment, with a proven track record of working independently and tackling complex, novel problems.
Collaborative Mindset: Demonstrated ability to work well within a team, share knowledge effectively, and contribute to a positive team environment.
Maintain a presence at the Sponsor Site – Houston, TX
Must have an active Top Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.
This position requires a minimum of 4 days a week on-site.

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s degree in Data Science, Cybersecurity, or related field with specialization in areas such as cryptocurrency analysis, blockchain forensics, or Dark Web intelligence.
Experience with programming languages (e.g., Python, R) for data analysis and automation.
Previous experience in monitoring and analyzing Dark Web forums and marketplaces.
Familiarity with intelligence-sharing platforms like ThreatConnect, OpenCTI, or MISP.
Experience with trusted AI or explainable AI techniques applied to cybersecurity and intelligence problems.
Technical Skills: Proficiency with tools and techniques used in threat intelligence, blockchain analysis, and open-source intelligence (OSINT), such as Maltego, Chainalysis, Palantir, or similar tools.
Cryptocurrency Knowledge: Strong understanding of cryptocurrency concepts, blockchain technology, and the role of cryptocurrencies in cybercrime.
Previous work experience in a classified environment, actively participating in cyber threat modeling, operational intelligence, or incident response.
Previous work experience performing (or providing data science support to) targeting analysis for HUMINT, cyber, and/or kinetic operations.

Top Secret

jobs.description:
About Us

Sophos is a cybersecurity leader defending 600,000 organizations globally with an AI-driven platform and expert-led services. Sophos meets organizations wherever they are in their security maturity and grows with them to defeat cyberattacks. Its solutions combine machine learning, automation, and real-time threat intelligence with frontline human expertise from Sophos X-Ops to deliver advanced, 24/7 threat monitoring, detection, and response.

Sophos offers industry-leading managed detection and response (MDR) alongside a comprehensive portfolio of cybersecurity technologies — including endpoint, network, email, and cloud security, extended detection and response (XDR), identity threat detection and response (ITDR), and next-gen SIEM. Together with expert advisory services, these capabilities help organizations proactively reduce risk and respond faster, with the visibility and scalability needed to stay ahead of evolving threats.

Sophos goes to market with a global partner ecosystem, including Managed Service Providers (MSPs), Managed Security Service Providers (MSSPs), resellers and distributors, marketplace integrations, and cyber risk partners, giving organizations the flexibility to choose trusted relationships when securing their business. Sophos is headquartered in Oxford, U.K. More information is available at www.sophos.com .

Role Summary

As a Threat Analyst - Tier II on our Managed Detection and Response (MDR) team, you will provide best-in-class monitoring, detection, and response services to proactively defend customer environments before attacks prevail. You will work alongside and contribute to a team of cyber threat hunters, incident response analysts, engineers, and ethical hackers by using enterprise, log analysis and endpoint collection systems to facilitate investigations, identification, and neutralization of cyber threats.

What You Will Do

Investigate and analyze logs and security-related events via Sophos tooling
Handle escalations from Tier I Threat Analysts - guide / advise on investigation handling
Onboard and train new Threat Analysts
Create cases, track and follow up with clients through threat neutralization
Communicate and document findings to various customer audiences including technical and executive teams
Follow up with customers through to issue resolution and drive continuous improvement by providing detailed recommendations to minimize risk in customer environments
Acknowledge and satisfy inbound customer requests and interact with customers through various mediums (Email, Phone, Ticket)
Collaborate and assist with core security and threat response teams
Actively research emerging Indicators of Compromise/Attack, exploits and vulnerabilities
Conduct threat hunting to identify potential threats throughout the MDR customer base
Participate in Security Operations process improvement and creation
Obtain metrics for reporting on threat trends, intelligence analysis and situational awareness

What You Will Bring

Essential:

2+ years of experience working in a SOC environment or computer security team in an IT environment
Endpoint and network security experience required; IDS, IPS, EDR, ATP, Malware defenses and monitoring experience
Experience with threat hunting
Experience administering and supporting Windows OS (workstations and server) and one of the following: Apple or Linux-based operating systems (RedHat, Debian, Ubuntu, OS X)
Knowledge of common adversary tactics and techniques, e.g., obfuscation, persistence, defense evasion, etc.
Fundamental understanding of network traffic analysis including TCP/IP, routing, switching, protocols, etc.
Strong understanding of Windows event log analysis
Working knowledge of incident response procedures
Passion for all things related to information technology and cybersecurity
Natural curiosity and ability to learn new skills quickly
Excellent troubleshooting and analytical skills, with proven ability to think outside the box
Customer service-oriented with strong written and verbal communication skills
Must thrive within a team environment as well as on an individual basis
Innovative mindset and driven to contribute to a team providing a best-in-class cybersecurity service
Bachelors in Information Technology, Computer Science or a related field; or relevant commensurate work experience
Willingness to work outside of standard business days including weekends and holidays – our MDR service is 24x7x365 (Hours are standard business hours)

Desirable

Knowledge of MITRE ATT&CK framework
Experience with SQL query construction
Experience with OSQuery Programming and scripting skills - proficient knowledge of PowerShell
Experience with enterprise information security data management - SIEM
Advanced Cyber Security certifications

Ready to Join Us?

At Sophos, we believe in the power of diverse perspectives to fuel innovation. Research shows that candidates sometimes hesitate to apply if they don't check every box in a job description. We challenge that notion. Your unique experiences and skills might be exactly what we need to enhance our team. Don't let a checklist hold you back – we encourage you to apply.

Thales people architect identity management and data protection solutions at the heart of digital security. Business and governments rely on us to bring trust to the billions of digital interactions they have with people. Our technologies and services help banks exchange funds, people cross borders, energy become smarter and much more. More than 30,000 organizations already rely on us to verify the identities of people and things, grant access to digital services, analyze vast quantities of information and encrypt data to make the connected world more secure.

Security Analyst

The Opportunity

As a Security Analyst, you will collaborate with a team of experienced security professionals to safeguard our corporate and production environments, leveraging advanced security tools and techniques to play a critical role in detecting, preventing, investigating, and responding to security threats and incidents.

As a first line of defense, you are expected to bring deep expertise across security operations, cloud security, DevSecOps, threat detection, and incident response, with strong hands-on experience in securing modern cloud-native environments. In addition, you will partner with cross-functional teams to provide security guidance, support, and training to strengthen our organization’s overall security posture.

This position requires participation in a shift rotation to support 24/7 security monitoring and incident response operations.

Responsibilities

Monitor, investigate, and triage security events to support and enhance threat modeling efforts
Proactively monitor cloud, network, endpoint to identify suspicious activity and emerging threats
Perform cloud security posture assessments, configuration reviews, policy enforcement, and continuous compliance monitoring across AWS, Azure, and GCP environments
Develop and maintain security alerts, log correlation rules, and dashboards using SIEM solution
Develop and implement security automation, detection engineering, and response workflows to improve operational efficiency and reduce manual effort
Configure, administer, and optimize security platforms including SIEM, CSPM, CNAPP, EDR/XDR, DLP, vulnerability management, and cloud security monitoring solutions
Conduct ongoing threat hunts and publish regular threat intelligence reports
Manage the InfoSec ticket queue, conduct investigations, and document resolutions
Review and evaluate vulnerability scan results and remediation efforts
Document, analyze, and escalate security incidents as needed
Collaborate with other business units to assess system configurations and ensure secure integration
Partner with internal stakeholders to define, develop, and implement security standards and best practices
Conduct quarterly security gap analyses and risk assessments
Conduct third-party security assessments for new and renewing vendors

Qualifications

5+ years of hands-on experience with major cloud service providers (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP)
5+ years of hands-on experience with endpoint security and detection technologies such as Cortex XDR, CrowdStrike, Microsoft Defender, or equivalent platforms.
5+ years of experience working with SIEM solutions, including log correlation, alert development, and dashboard creation
5+ years of experience in security alert monitoring and incident investigation
3+ years of hands-on experience implementing DevSecOps practices, including security integration within CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), container security, and automated security testing
Strong understanding of cloud-native security tools and configurations, including identity and access management, logging/monitoring, and workload protection
Experience developing automation using scripting languages such as Python, PowerShell, Bash, or similar to improve security operations and incident response workflows
Practical experience with threat hunting techniques and methodologies
Familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework and its application to detection engineering and incident analysis
Strong ability to interpret and analyze security logs, network traffic, and system behaviors to detect attack patterns and anomalies
In-depth knowledge of network, endpoint, and cloud security technologies and principles
Demonstrated experience collaborating across global teams and working in cross-functional environments
Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to work independently
Up-to-date knowledge of recent vulnerabilities, attack vectors, and remediation strategies
Excellent written and verbal communication skills to support collaboration with technical and non-technical stakeholders
Experience administering and fine-tuning security infrastructure is a strong plus
Security professional certifications such as CISSP, CCSP, Security+, GSEC, GCIH, GCIA, AWS Security Specialty, Azure Security Engineer Associate, or equivalent certifications are preferred

Position Description

The best version of us starts with You!

We CGI is looking for passionate and detail-oriented Security Analysts to join our team supporting a leading global Banking client.

The role involves vulnerability remediation and large-scale patch deployment following heightened regulatory focus on AI-enabled cyber threats. The initiative supports cyber hygiene, operational resilience and safe continuity of client’s business services.

Selected candidates will lead the organization’s vulnerability response capability, ensuring vulnerabilities are rapidly identified, assessed, prioritized, remediated, and governed. The role is responsible for reducing cyber risk exposure by coordinating remediation efforts across infrastructure, cloud, application, and technology teams while ensuring compliance with internal policies, regulatory requirements, and remediation SLAs.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Manage the end-to-end vulnerability response and remediation lifecycle, from identification and assessment through remediation, validation, and closure.

Lead and coordinate vulnerability remediation activities across infrastructure, application, cloud, network, and other technology teams.

Ensure Critical and High-risk vulnerabilities are remediated within established Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and organizational risk tolerances.

Drive accelerated response and remediation activities for actively exploited vulnerabilities, zero-day vulnerabilities, and emerging security threats.

Collaborate with technology and business stakeholders to track remediation progress, resolve blockers, and manage exceptions or risk acceptances where required.

Monitor vulnerability remediation performance and maintain accurate tracking, status updates, risk assessments, and remediation records.

Significant experience in Vulnerability Management, Cyber Security Operations, or Cyber Defense.

Experience managing technology risk and remediation governance.

Exposure to regulatory environments such as:

NIST SP 800 40
DORA

You will design and oversee field work related to monitoring, investigating, and remediating contaminated sites impacted by hydrocarbons (diesel, gasoline crude oil etc.) fertilizers and metals, as well as prepare technical reports. Position Purpose：
The Sales Operations Analyst will be responsible for supporting the daily execution of passenger vehicle sales operations in Chile, ensuring accurate order processing, effective coordination with logistics partners and distributors, proper management of commercial incentives, and reliable operational reporting.
Key Responsibilities
1. Sales Order Management
- Register, process, and monitor vehicle sales orders in the company's internal systems.
- Track order status and ensure timely updates throughout the sales and delivery process.
- Maintain accurate and updated sales information across relevant platforms.
- Identify and escalate order discrepancies, delays, and operational issues.
- Coordinate with internal teams to ensure efficient order processing.
2. Logistics & Distributor Coordination
- Coordinate with local logistics teams, warehouses, and distributors to support vehicle delivery operations.
- Monitor vehicle availability, order fulfillment, and delivery status.
- Follow up on pending orders and resolve operational issues with relevant stakeholders.
- Maintain effective communication with logistics providers and dealer networks.
- Support the alignment between sales orders, inventory availability, and delivery schedules.
3. Commercial Incentives & Expense Management
- Calculate and validate commercial bonuses, dealer incentives, KPI-related payments, and other expenses according to established business policies.
- Review and process special commercial approvals and OEM-related incentives when applicable.
- Verify supporting documentation and ensure accuracy of calculations.
- Coordinate with Sales and Finance teams regarding incentive validation and payment processes.
- Maintain accurate records of commercial incentives, approvals, and related expenses.
4. Data Management & Operational Reporting
- Collect, consolidate, and maintain operational data from different internal systems.
- Prepare periodic sales operations reports and performance summaries.
- Monitor operational indicators related to orders, deliveries, incentives, and commercial activities.
- Identify data inconsistencies and support corrective actions.
- Provide accurate and timely information to the Operations Manager and relevant stakeholders.
5. Cross-functional Coordination & Process Improvement
- Collaborate with Sales, Logistics, Finance, and other departments to ensure efficient operational processes.
- Support the implementation and continuous improvement of internal procedures.
- Identify opportunities to improve reporting accuracy, process efficiency, and operational controls.
- Assist with operational documentation, internal reviews, and business-related administrative requirements.
- Support additional operational activities assigned by the Operations Manager.

Education
- Bachelor's degree or professional qualification in Business Administration, Commercial Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Logistics, International Business, or a related field.
Professional Experience
- Minimum 1 year of experience in Sales Operations, Commercial Administration, Logistics Coordination, Business Analysis, or related functions.

- Experience working with distributors, dealer networks, or multinational companies is an advantage.

- Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including pivot tables, formulas, and data analysis.
- Experience using ERP, CRM, or sales management systems is desirable.
- Ability to organize, validate, and analyze commercial and operational information.
- Knowledge of sales order management, inventory coordination, and commercial reporting.
- Experience with Power BI or other reporting tools is an advantage.
Language Requirements
- Spanish: Fluent.
- English: Upper-intermediate or advanced, with the ability to communicate effectively in a professional environment.
Other Requirements
- Valid driver's license.
- Availability for occasional visits to warehouses, distributors, or other operational locations when required.

jobs.description:
Description

Business Analyst in Network Strategy and Performance owns processes & analytics that directly shape how Amazon serves customers globally. They are an analytical problem solver who is comfortable in a fast-paced, multi-tasked, high-energy environment. They are self-motivated, operating independently in an autonomous environment to deliver an exceptional customer experience with little to no guidance. They operationalize the long- and short-term staffing plans, working cross-functionally with site Operations, planning teams, training, finance, and others. They will contribute to the team's AI-driven transformation agenda by applying AI tools to increase the speed, quality, and scale of analytical outputs. They do not just report or fix defects, but think critically about why they happen, what surrounds them, and how to prevent them — combining analytical rigor with a proactive, anticipatory mindset.

Key job responsibilities

Create and accurately maintain CSA shift schedules ensuring shifts are optimally planned to meet the sites short term forecast requirements and Service Levels (SL).
Monitor actual staffing levels against planned staffing and take the relevant corrective actions as required improve SL.
Effectively plan and monitor CSA adherence to assigned schedule, including productive and non-productive activities.
Work closely with mid to senior-level leaders across core teams to identify and mitigate emerging risks and assists in creating mitigation plans for staffing corrections and SL recovery.
Responsible for coordinating site-staffing needs including reporting and analysis of site headcount numbers as per staffing plan.
Understanding and monitor symptoms of CSA burnout, detecting the metrics that can signal these symptoms and assist in implementing interventions to eliminate outlier experiences.
Responsible to coordinate various cross-training, new-hires, and management of network and site-wide shift rotation processes as per business need.
Create work schedules for associates, identifies and proactively resolves headcount deficiencies and overages.
Investigate defects and operational anomalies to identify systemic drivers (system-related, behavioral, or shared responsibility), not just symptoms. Highlight and communicate metrics impacting the operation that could impact service levels, customer experience, and business process.
Build and maintain validation checks, dashboards, and automated alerts to catch defects early — before they impact customers or operations.
Independently apply AI tools (e.g., Amazon Q, generative AI assistants, AgentZ) to accelerate analytical workflows, identifying opportunities to improve speed and quality of outputs.
Apply AI tools to develop automation for repetitive tasks within your workstream, demonstrating measurable productivity improvement.

About The Team

The Network Strategy and Performance (NP) team defines and delivers the right human-assisted support to Amazon customers under demand and labor supply volatility, by optimizing the Amazon Customer Service (CS) network for customer experience, associate experience, and cost. We are responsible for: (1) planning customer support staffing; (2) preserving the customer experience when customers contact Customer Service; and (3) ensuring best costs for providing customer support.

We analyse historical data and anticipate potential business events to accurately predict the number of Customer Service Associates (CSAs) required for a given period. Our areas of expertise span forecasting, planning, optimization, data analytics, and reporting. We deliver our vision using operations research, data science, and program management — and we continue to challenge the status quo, invent and simplify, and deliver excellence for our customers.

The Network Performance team is on a transformation journey. We are building a future-ready team that combines analytical rigor with AI fluency, executive-level communication, and the ability to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries. We are seeking a Business Analyst to join this team and help shape how Amazon plans, staff, and optimizes its Customer Service network.

Basic Qualifications

1+ years of tax, finance or a related analytical field experience
2+ years of complex Excel VBA macros writing experience
Bachelor's degree or equivalent
Experience defining requirements and using data and metrics to draw business insights
Experience with SQL or ETL

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with Tableau
Experience using very large datasets

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. jobs.title: Geological Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
Upstream Data Analyst

Denver, Colorado
Petro-Hunt, L.L.C., a Dallas, Texas mid-sized independent Oil and Gas Exploration Company, is seeking an Upstream Data Analyst for its Denver, Colorado office.

About Petro-Hunt, L.L.C.

Petro-Hunt, L.L.C. is a privately held independent oil and gas company headquartered in Dallas, Texas. Owned and operated by the William Herbert Hunt family, Petro-Hunt and its affiliates are actively engaged in various industries with a primary focus in the oil and gas industry.
Our company traces its roots to the 1920s, when the legendary H.L. Hunt entered the oil and gas business in El Dorado, Arkansas, and later played an active role in developing the East Texas Oil Field from the drill test of the Daisy Bradford #3.
Today, Petro-Hunt is a Top 10 Private Liquids Producer in the U.S. with operations in six states. We are more than just an oil and gas company — Petro-Hunt actively purchases minerals and royalties, owns and operates a gas processing facility, is part owner of an oil refinery, actively invests in real estate development, and operates a private equity alternative investment division.

Job Summary

Our Denver office generates and consumes a large amount of data — well logs and subsurface interpretations, daily drilling and completion reports, and production and operations history — and much of it lives in separate systems that do not talk to each other. The Upstream Data Analyst exists to close that gap.
This is a hands-on, analyst-leaning role for someone who is equally comfortable writing a query, wiring two databases together, and presenting a chart that changes a decision. You will pull data from across the drilling, completions, production, and geoscience domains, reconcile it into something trustworthy, and turn it into analysis that geologists, engineers, and management actually use. Just as importantly, you will look for the parts of that work that should not be done by hand twice and automate them — increasingly with the help of AI tooling.
We are looking for curiosity and technical range for this position. If you want to avoid doing repetitive tasks and look forward to digging into the data and databases and creating workflows to answer complex questions, we would like to talk to you.

Key Responsibilities

Data Integration

Connect and reconcile data across disparate upstream systems — drilling and completions reporting (e.g., WellView, Corva), production and operations databases (e.g., P2 Carte), geoscience projects (e.g., Kingdom Suite, GeoGraphix), commercial data vendors (e.g., Enverus, S&P), state regulatory databases, and internal accounting and land systems.
Build and maintain repeatable pipelines that move data between these systems so analysis starts from one trusted source rather than a fresh export.
Migrate and synchronize data between geoscience platforms, corporate databases, and vendor exports, preserving data integrity and auditability along the way.
Resolve the identity problems that make upstream data hard: API number formats, well and completion naming conventions, wellbore vs. producing-entity relationships, and unit and datum inconsistencies.

Analysis and Reporting

Answer real business questions with data — well performance benchmarking, decline behavior as related to geologic variations, and offset operator activity.
Build dashboards, recurring reports, and one-off analyses for geoscience and management audiences.
Present findings clearly to technical and non-technical staff, including the assumptions and data limitations behind them.

Automation and AI

Identify manual, repetitive workflows across the office and replace them with scripted or automated processes.
Apply AI tools — large language models, coding assistants, and data analysis assistants — to accelerate development and deal evaluation, extract information from unstructured sources such as scanned reports and PDFs, and shorten the path from question to answer.
Evaluate new tooling pragmatically and help the office adopt what actually works.

Geoscience Platform and Data Stewardship

Administer geoscience interpretation projects and databases (GeoGraphix strongly preferred; Kingdom Suite or Petra experience considered) — project creation and maintenance, well and log data loading, formation tops, directional surveys, and backup/recovery.
Maintain the health of the geoscience database environment, including direct database-level access for querying, QC, and bulk updates.

Data Quality and Governance

Own the QC of the datasets you build: validate spatial and attribute data, including coordinate reference systems, well headers, directional surveys, and allocation logic.
Document data sources, definitions, and transformations so results are reproducible and auditable.
Help develop and enforce practical data standards and naming conventions across the Denver office.

Cross-Functional Support

Work directly with geologists to support daily workflows and project work.
Serve as the go-to technical resource for geologists’ day-to-day software and data issues.
Serve as a liaison between technical staff and the IT and corporate data groups in Dallas.
Support the preparation of exhibits and data packages for regulatory hearings and internal reviews.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, Geology, GIS, Earth Sciences, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.

Experience

3+ years of relevant technical experience. Candidates with upstream oil and gas experience will be considered at a commensurate level; exceptional early-career candidates who can demonstrate substantial self-directed technical work may also be considered.

Technical Skills

Strong SQL and hands-on experience querying and joining data across relational databases; experience querying vendor application databases directly (e.g., SAP SQL Anywhere/Sybase, SQL Server) is a strong plus.
Proficiency in Python for data work (pandas, or equivalent), including reading and writing common industry formats such as LAS, CSV, and vendor exports.
Experience building visualizations and dashboards (e.g., Power BI, Spotfire, Tableau, or Python-based tools).
Comfort with GIS concepts and tools (e.g., ArcGIS, QGIS), including coordinate reference systems and spatial joins.
Version control (Git) and general software hygiene are a plus.

AI Proficiency

Demonstrated ability to leverage AI tools — large language models, coding assistants, and data analysis assistants — to streamline complex tasks, automate workflows, and enhance productivity. We use these tools daily and expect this person to help us use them better.

Preferred Skills

Working knowledge of upstream oil and gas data: well logs, drilling and completion reporting, production allocation, 2D/3D seismic, and other subsurface data types.
Hands-on administration of a geoscience interpretation platform — GeoGraphix strongly preferred — including its underlying data model and import/export formats.
Experience with commercial data products (Enverus, IHS/S&P, TGS) and state regulatory data sources (NDIC, COGCC/ECMC, RRC).
Exposure to cloud data platforms or modern data stack tooling.
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication; able to explain a result and defend the method behind it.
A bias toward automating the boring parts and a low tolerance for doing the same thing twice.

What We Offer

Fast-paced, well-funded, aggressive work environment in a stable, private company
Direct exposure to decision-makers and real influence over how the office works with data

Highly competitive benefit programs
8% 401K match
Parking provided

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - Frontier AI Data Labeling
jobs.description:
About The Role

Frontier models are only as good as the data they learn from. At Hippocratic AI, that data decides whether an AI agent safely guides a patient through a medication change at 2 a.m.

Our data powers Polaris, a constellation of models with a 700B-parameter core and specialized safety supervisors. In our evaluations, Polaris reaches 99.95% accuracy on drug-safety benchmarks versus 87.9% for the closest voice-deployable frontier model. The labeling, evals, and rater calibration behind it are how we earn and defend numbers like that.

We’re hiring a Technical Program Manager to run the human-in-the-loop data labeling engine behind our frontier healthcare AI. That spans audio and conversation annotation, clinician-labeled training data, preference and RLHF data, and the evaluations that decide what ships. You’ll work daily with ML researchers, applied scientists, and licensed clinicians. The data you produce feeds directly into our model training and evaluation loops.

What You’ll Do

Run the data pipelines behind our models. Own end-to-end delivery of labeling and annotation programs, including audio and voice-conversation labeling, supervised labeling, and preference and RLHF data. You’ll manage scoping, task design, execution, QA, and delivery against live model-development cycles.
Turn evals into products. Work with ML and Applied Science to turn evaluation and training-signal needs into concrete labeling tasks, rubrics, and success criteria. Your evals become the benchmarks that gate releases.
Build and scale an expert rater workforce. Source, screen, and onboard clinicians and specialized raters through marketplaces, vendors, and in-house teams. This includes designing qualification tasks, setting rates, and scaling pools up and down as programs change.
Write the guidelines that shape model behavior. Author and iterate labeling guidelines and annotation rubrics, especially for subjective, high-stakes clinical judgment.
Engineer data quality at scale. Design QC systems using gold sets, calibration sessions, spot checks, and inter-rater agreement tracking. Catch rater drift and annotation bottlenecks before they reach training.
Drive velocity and accountability. Track throughput, cost, and quality. Manage vendor relationships (SOWs, performance reviews), choose labeling and QA tooling, and keep Engineering, Clinical, and Infrastructure aligned on dependencies and timelines.

What Success Looks Like

By Day 90: You own a live data labeling or eval program through a major delivery milestone. You’ve cleared a critical bottleneck in the pipeline and shipped one measurable quality or throughput improvement.
By 12 months: You run multiple concurrent labeling and eval programs. Your calibrated rater bench is trusted by ML teams, and you can trace model improvements back to the data you delivered.

What You Bring

5+ years in technical program management or data operations in an AI/ML or data-intensive environment (3+ years considered for exceptional candidates)
2+ years hands-on with data labeling, annotation, or model evaluation, including writing guidelines and managing quality at scale
Experience sourcing and managing contractor or expert annotator workforces through marketplaces (e.g., Mercor, Upwork, Toloka) or labeling vendors
Working knowledge of how annotation quality affects model training, including preference data, pairwise comparisons, and rater calibration (RLHF)
A strong grasp of quality metrics (IAA, precision/recall on gold sets, throughput vs. accuracy tradeoffs)
A track record of owning critical data or eval projects under time pressure, working with ML engineers and applied scientists, and driving results without direct authority
Comfort with ambiguity in a fast-moving, healthcare-adjacent AI environment

Nice to Have

Experience running or supporting RLHF or other training-data pipelines at an AI lab or applied ML team
Clinical, healthcare, or other regulated, high-stakes data experience
Familiarity with Label Studio, Scale AI, Surge AI, or SageMaker Ground Truth
Experience qualifying specialized raters such as clinicians or bilingual SMEs
Exposure to reward hacking and specification gaming, and how annotation design can mitigate them

Why Join Hippocratic AI

Reinvent healthcare with AI that puts safety first.
We’re building the world’s first healthcare‑only, safety‑focused LLM — a breakthrough platform designed to transform patient outcomes at a global scale. This is category creation.

Work with the people shaping the future.
Hippocratic AI was co‑founded by CEO Munjal Shah and a team of physicians, hospital leaders, AI pioneers, and researchers from institutions like El Camino Health, Johns Hopkins, Washington University in St. Louis, Stanford, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and NVIDIA.

Backed by the world’s leading healthcare and AI investors.
We recently raised a $126M Series C at a $3.5B valuation, led by Avenir Growth, bringing total funding to $404M with participation from CapitalG, General Catalyst, a16z, Kleiner Perkins, Premji Invest, UHS, Cincinnati Children’s, WellSpan Health, John Doerr, Rick Klausner, and others.

Build alongside the best in healthcare and AI.
Join experts who’ve spent their careers improving care, advancing science, and building world‑changing technologies — ensuring our platform is powerful, trusted, and truly transformative.

Equal Opportunity

jobs.title: Sr Program Manager, AI & Data, Global Corporate Communications
jobs.description:
Description

Amazon Global Corporate Communications (GCC) is looking for a Senior Program Manager to lead the data and AI systems that GCC's teams rely on. You'll build the shared foundation beneath GCC's work: making its data usable by AI, delivering the AI systems on top of it, and connecting the work across GCC and its partners.

Today, a lot of GCC's most valuable data is scattered. Research, media coverage, agency reporting, processes, and planning documents live in different places and formats, with different access. That makes it hard for teams to bring it together, and hard for AI to do anything with it. You'll connect those sources, structure them so AI can actually retrieve and reason over the content, and design tools on top of them. The teams who produce the data still own it. You make sure it's structured, accessible, and fits together, so everyone gets more out of it.

A lot of this job comes down to giving people across the team more ownership of their work. That happens two ways. First, by reducing dependencies, the places where people are stuck waiting on a manual step, a handoff, or the one person who knows how something works. Second, by clearing away the rote, repetitive work that fills their days. You'll get to know how GCC operates, find where both of these slow people down, and build what it takes to help. Everyone here is a builder, and your job is to support that.

No two months in this role look the same. The data keeps growing, the tools keep changing, and there's always a new challenge worth taking on. It's a great fit for someone who likes to work independently, dig into complex problems, and see their work make a difference across a team.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience implementing repeatable processes and driving automation or standardization
Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
Experience in complex problem solving, and working in a tight schedule environment

new_jobs.description:
Project Manager
| Launch & Scale Operations
Skye Health | Full-Time, W-2 | Remote
Position Overview

● Skye Health is seeking a hands-on Project Manager to support the launch and scaling of its telehealth business. This role spans multiple interconnected workstreams across operations, clinical support, technology, Customer Service, hiring, vendors, and implementation.
● The Project Manager will work closely with Skye’s Head of Operations to create structure, clarify priorities and ownership, and keep important initiatives moving to completion. The role is best suited for someone who can quickly understand a fast-moving environment, identify where coordination or follow-through is breaking down, and create practical systems without adding unnecessary process.
Employment & Working Model
• This is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week role working closely with Skye’s Head of Operations and cross-functional teams. The Project Manager will gain broad exposure to key workstreams, take ownership of follow-through, and help create the structure and operating systems needed as Skye launches and scales.
• Compensation: $80,000 annual salary, plus benefits.
Key Responsibilities

Launch & Cross-Functional Project Management
• Maintain a clear view of active launch and scale workstreams, including priorities, owners, timelines, dependencies, risks, decisions, and next steps.
• Coordinate across teams and partners to keep work moving, clarify ownership, and ensure important actions and follow-up are completed.
• Identify blockers, gaps, competing priorities, or issues requiring leadership attention and surface them at the right time.
Operational Partnership & Leadership Support
• Work closely with leadership to understand how work moves, where time is being consumed, and where additional structure or follow-through is needed.
• Organize information and coordination across meetings, messages, workstreams, and stakeholders so ownership and next steps remain clear.
• Help protect leadership bandwidth by routing work appropriately, reducing unnecessary one-off interruptions, and coordinating internal and external resources.
Implementation & Transition Management
• Support major implementations and transitions by keeping milestones, dependencies, testing, handoffs, ownership, and open items visible and moving through completion.
• Coordinate across internal teams, external partners, and new resources to surface risks, resolve gaps, and ensure key workflows and implementation issues are addressed before they become recurring operational problems.
Systems, AI & Automation
• Identify recurring manual work, repeated questions, and process friction that can be standardized, automated, or supported with better tools.
• Use AI, automation, templates, and workflow improvements to increase internal efficiency and translate recurring operational needs into clear requirements for technical teams.
• Partner with the appropriate clinical, operational, and technical owners to ensure AI-supported workflows reflect approved content, business rules, and escalation boundaries.
Hiring, Onboarding & Team Coordination
• Support hiring and onboarding logistics as needed, including candidate coordination, follow-up, and onboarding plans.
• Help new team members, contractors, and other resources integrate smoothly with clear responsibilities, priorities, documentation, dependencies, and handoffs.
Metrics & Continuous Improvement
• Identify recurring operational issues and opportunities to improve how work moves across teams.
• Help establish practical operating metrics and dashboards that give leadership visibility into launch, scale, workload, and execution.
• Clarify where key data lives, who owns it, and which measures are useful enough to drive action rather than create reporting for reporting’s sake.
Role Boundaries
• Coordinate and operationalize cross-functional work without replacing the clinical, legal, compliance, technical, or other subject-matter owners responsible for substantive decisions.
• The role will evolve as Skye Health launches and scales, with priorities reviewed regularly with leadership.
Qualifications

Required
• Demonstrated experience managing cross-functional projects or operations in a fast-moving organization.
• Experience working in a startup, high-growth, or similarly dynamic environment where priorities and processes are still evolving.
• Strong ability to create structure, clarify ownership, and move work forward with limited direction.
• Excellent organization, follow-through, judgment, and attention to detail.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize input from multiple stakeholders and work independently with senior leaders.
Preferred
• Digital health, telehealth, healthcare operations, or other regulated-industry experience.
• Experience coordinating technology implementations, cross-functional operational work, or vendor transitions.
• Experience building workflows, SOPs, automations, internal systems, or operational dashboards and metrics.
• Experience using AI and automation to improve operational efficiency.
Success in This Role
• Success means Skye Health has a clear operating rhythm as it launches and scales: priorities and ownership are visible, cross-functional work stays on track, and leadership has better visibility into what is moving, what is blocked, and what needs attention.
• Over time, the role should reduce the amount of day-to-day coordination leadership has to personally manage while helping the organization operate with greater clarity, consistency, and follow-through.

This role is intended for experienced systems and embedded software leaders—including software engineering managers, technical leads, or senior architects—who have led datacenter server and platform software programs and can operate as a trusted technical partner to hyperscale CSP engineering teams.

As a member of the CSP Engagements team, you will act as the primary technical engagement leader between NVIDIA’s system software organizations and CSP platform, system software, and AI teams, ensuring alignment, readiness, and successful large‑scale deployment of NVIDIA‑based datacenter solutions.

What You Will Be Doing

Lead deep technical engagements with hyperscale CSPs as the primary NVIDIA point of contact for system software, firmware, and platform readiness for NVIDIA datacenter products.
Partner directly with CSP system software, firmware, and infrastructure engineering leaders to align on software architecture, bring‑up plans, deployment readiness, and production requirements for NVIDIA‑based server and rack‑scale platforms.
Represent CSP technical priorities internally, advocating for customer requirements and tradeoffs across NVIDIA’s system software, firmware, hardware, silicon, and product teams are aligned to customer needs, timelines, and constraints.
Own the end‑to‑end CSP engagement lifecycle, from early technical alignment and pre‑production readiness through large‑scale deployment, escalation management, and sustained production support.
Drive bi‑directional technical communication: translating CSP system‑level requirements into actionable focus areas for NVIDIA engineering teams, while clearly communicating NVIDIA platform capabilities, tradeoffs, and limitations back to customers.
Proactively identify and manage cross‑company technical risks affecting CSP deployments, including OS enablement, firmware maturity, observability, reliability, and hardware/software integration challenges.
Support rack‑scale and multi‑rack datacenter deployments by working closely with CSP infrastructure teams and NVIDIA engineering stakeholders to ensure system software readiness and operational success at hyperscale.

What We Need To See

This role requires strong technical depth and leadership credibility in systems software.

Strong background in systems or embedded software, with experience across Linux kernel/drivers, server firmware (BMC/BIOS/UEFI), or datacenter platform bring‑up and hardware/software interfaces.

Experience working directly with hyperscale CSP engineering teams on deep technical topics, including bring up, performance, reliability, observability, and deployment readiness.
Strong ability to operate as a technical leader and influencer, aligning senior engineers, architects, and executives across organizational and company boundaries.
BS or MS in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent experience.
10+ years of experience in systems software, embedded software, or datacenter server development, including leadership responsibility

Direct experience with NVIDIA GB200 and/or GB300 platforms, including hands‑on or leadership involvement in system software, firmware, or platform enablement efforts.
Experience driving or supporting CSP-facing engagements specifically for NVIDIA datacenter platforms, translating GB200 / GB300 software and firmware capabilities into production‑ready solutions.
Familiarity with the end‑to‑end NVIDIA data center software stack, including system software bring‑up, platform integration, observability, reliability, and deployment considerations at hyperscale.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact
Axon Community Connect enables public safety agencies to build voluntary, policy-based partnerships with businesses and community members. Through camera registration and secure camera integration, the program expands investigative reach and real-time situational awareness during critical incidents while maintaining privacy, transparency, and camera-owner control.
As the PSO Program Manager, Community Connect, you will lead the operational health and scalable execution of the Community Connect program across Axon’s U.S. customer base and growing international footprint.
You will establish the operating discipline that enables Program Coordinators to deliver consistent agency outcomes. This includes maintaining visibility into program performance, work-order health, delivery dependencies, technical readiness, and customer-impacting risks; strengthening the processes, tools, and playbooks used across the team; and ensuring complex issues receive the appropriate cross-functional attention.
You will serve as a program-level escalation resource, coordinating with Professional Services, Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, and Finance to remove blockers and drive resolution. You will also provide consultative support for hardware deployment readiness, remote hardware configuration and activation, connectivity, and camera integration requirements.
Your work will enable agencies to launch and sustain Community Connect programs that extend operational visibility, strengthen community participation, and scale responsibly without compromising privacy or the customer experience.

Remote

Proficiency with CRM, project-management, and workflow tools such as Salesforce, Smartsheet, Jira, or similar platforms, as well as Microsoft Office and Google Workspace.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager - Customer Trust & Governance - Public Sector/Government
new_jobs.description:
The Technical Program Manager: Customer Trust & Governance - Public/Government will support Nutanix's Customer Trust and security programs by participating in compliance auditing, maintaining customer due diligence assets, proactively monitoring evolving customer and regulatory requirements applicable to Nutanix’s ability to participate in the global marketplace, and helping to operationalize and scale customer trust operations. The role combines system and software security expertise, customer-assurance experience, framework/compliance auditing, and program management to ensure Nutanix’s security, privacy, product compliance, AI governance, and public sector/global government representations to external stakeholders remains accurate, supportable, consistent, and aligned with evolving customer, industry, and regulatory expectations.

The position partners closely with Product Security, Information Security, Sales, Customer Support, Privacy, Legal, Product Compliance, and other stakeholders to support customer diligence activities, strategic transactions, the Nutanix Industrial Security Program and Customer Trust Center operations.

Key Responsibilities

Maintain operations and strategy for Customer Trust led initiatives and operations.
Partner with stakeholders to identify, assess, and communicate the business impact of evolving customer assurance requirements, cybersecurity expectations, compliance requirements, and emerging regulatory obligations.
Maintain and improve customer-facing customer trust assets, including approved content, evidence packages, attestations, and trust-center materials.
Support the Nutanix Industrial Security Program compliance including assessments and implementation of controls against frameworks such as NIST 800-171 and/or CMMC.
Support complex customer security and compliance assessments, including questionnaires, evidence reviews, findings responses, and customer assurance discussions.
Review customer-facing security, privacy, compliance, and AI governance representations for accuracy, consistency, supportability, and alignment with approved certifications, attestations, policies, and control documentation.
Develop scalable processes, knowledge resources, and operating procedures to improve customer trust operations.
Manage outsourced customer trust analyst enablement, quality review, and continuous improvement efforts for outsourced assessment support.
Support strategic customer opportunities and complex diligence activities and partner with multiple Nutanix teams to coordinate cross-functional responses.
Track and communicate trends, recurring customer requirements, operational metrics, and areas for process improvement.
Partner with Sales, Legal, Product Security, Information Security, Privacy, Customer Support, and other stakeholders to support customer trust requirements.

Required Qualifications

7+ years of experience in cybersecurity, GRC, technology regulatory compliance/governance, technology risk, framework based compliance, or related fields.
U.S. Citizen and eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance if required to support government, defense, or other security-sensitive customer opportunities.
Experience supporting compliance and security for a technology company that sells to US Federal and Defense entities.
Experience supporting complex enterprise and public sector customer security assessments and customer due diligence activities including working knowledge of GRC portals and third party risk processes.
Direct experience providing program management for information security and compliance frameworks such as NIST, FedRAMP, SOC, ISO, CMMC, CSA Star, and a strong aptitude for learning regulatory requirements or new frameworks.
Experience participating in technical assessments and audits for a major compliance effort.
Ability to evaluate security documentation, certifications, policies, audit materials, and supporting evidence and translate these into controls applicable to customer requirements.
Build, maintain, and communicate detailed reporting and present findings to support decision-making and strategy.
Actively make recommendations for opportunities to collaborate more efficiently, scale processes using existing tools and systems, and own responsibility for implementing these solutions to help yield higher sales velocity, internal productivity, quality, and cost savings.
Ability to clearly identify, explain, and communicate progress, status, expectations, dependencies, and risks to executives, business partners and team members.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, as well as strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Experience working in a large, complex enterprise and partnering with Security, Legal, Privacy, Product and other stakeholders on commercial transactions.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting compliance and security control maintenance for a US public technology company with a global distribution chain and operations.
Bachelor's degree in information technology, cybersecurity, risk management, or equivalent work experience.
Experience supporting industry participation in global defense programs.
Experience reviewing security and information technology contract terms.
Direct experience with technology system implementation, security for on-premise and hosted systems, and operations within an enclaved compliance environment.
Experience supporting global, regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, public sector, or critical infrastructure.
CISSP, CIPT, CompTIA, or similar certifications.
Experience owning the management of GRC/Compliance tools, trust-center content, and vendor management.

Business Justification

Customer Trust has become an increasingly important revenue-enablement function as Nutanix expands within highly regulated and security-sensitive industries. Customer security and compliance assessment volume increased from 34 assessments in 2024 to 72 assessments in 2025 and more than 175 assessments as of September 30 2026. Customer requests are also becoming more complex, particularly in areas such as cybersecurity, AI governance, privacy, supply-chain risk, and regulatory compliance. Additionally, the Nutanix Industrial Security Program and related compliance frameworks that are mandatory to maintain are critical to selling into the US Federal/defense and global defense customer base.

Customer Trust currently relies on a limited number of resources to support rapidly growing customer diligence demands including time sensitive sales transactions that directly result in revenue. This new role is being added to provide additional support for customer assurance, cybersecurity governance, the Nutanix industrial security program, and enabling the Customer Trust program to scale more effectively against our global growth in customers and regulatory requirements.

Without additional capacity, Nutanix risks continuing to address a growing strategic workload through reactive, person-dependent processes rather than through a scalable and appropriately governed Customer Trust program.

Why a New Role Is Needed

This Role Will

Support complex and strategic customer diligence activities.
Improve the accuracy, consistency, and scalability of customer trust responses.
Scale, maintain and expand reusable customer trust assets and trust-center content and implement automation.
Increase the effectiveness of outsourced assessment support.
Provide deeper cybersecurity and GRC expertise for validating customer-facing security and compliance representations.
Help reduce transaction friction and support revenue-generating opportunities.

This is a new role created to provide additional capacity within the Customer Trust organization and to provide dedicated support for US Federal and global government sales as well as the Nutanix industrial security program. The role will have autonomy to accelerate automation and scalable customer practices using existing tools, and more efficient collaboration across cross-functional teams. It will also require experience with cybersecurity and compliance, independent judgment, program management, customer-facing assurance experience, and the ability to collaborate with the Customer Trust team to validate complex customer trust representations and supporting evidence.

Work Arrangement

This role operates in a hybrid capacity, blending the benefits of remote work with the advantages of in-person collaboration, Located in Durham, NC. For most roles, that will mean coming into an office a minimum of 2 - 3 days per week, however certain roles and/or teams may require more frequent in-office presence. Additional team-specific guidance and norms will be provided by your manager. This role is also available remotely.

The pay range for this position at commencement of employment is expected to be between USD $121,000 and USD $241,000 per year.

However, base pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements, including a sign-on bonus, restricted stock units, and discretionary awards in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits (including 401(k) eligibility and various paid time off benefits, such as vacation, sick time, and parental leave), dependent on the position offered. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base salary (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors. 5+ years of experience in Sea Logistics, Freight Forwarding, Supply Chain Management, Operational Key Account Management, Program Management, or Order Management environments.

At Kuehne+Nagel we strive daily to inspire, empower, and deliver not only to our customers, but also to our colleagues. Oracle Health Government Services is seeking a skilled Senior Federal Project Manager to join our mission-drive organization. In this role, you will be responsible for leading program activities to ensure the successful delivery of large, complex federal task orders. As a project management professional and leading contributor, you will provide high-quality operational and project management support to ensure projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with contractual requirements. This role requires the ability to independently assess priorities, oversee project activities, and maintain alignment with key program objectives. Working closely with federal customers, delivery teams, and program leadership, you will help manage customer expectations, minimize risk, and ensure project deliverables consistently meet or exceed quality standards.

You will provide strategic operations support by coordinating with stakeholders, preparing leadership and customer-facing materials, facilitating meetings, tracking action items, and maintaining alignment across multiple workstreams. You will analyze business needs and apply Oracle methodologies, policies, industry best practices, and product knowledge to help ensure solutions align with customer objectives. The ideal candidate is a dynamic, results-driven project manager who is highly organized, possesses strong communication and business acumen, and thrives in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.

Responsibilities

Support the Task Order Owner and/or Lead Project Manager in managing the tasks required for the end-to-end contractual delivery of large, complex task orders.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Academic Flourishing Initiative (AFI), Human Flourishing Program
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

Why join the Harvard Faculty of Arts and Sciences?

The Faculty of Arts and Sciences (FAS) is the historic heart of Harvard University. It is the home of Harvard’s undergraduate program (Harvard College, founded in 1636) as well as all of Harvard’s Ph.D. programs (the Harvard Kenneth C. Griffin Graduate School of Arts and Sciences, founded in 1872), Harvard Athletics and the Division of Continuing Education. The 40 academic departments and 30+ centers of the FAS support a community unparalleled in its academic excellence across the broadest range of liberal arts and sciences disciplines. Together, the FAS seeks to foster an environment of ambition, curiosity and shared commitment to knowledge and truth that elicits excellence from all members of our community and prepares the next generation of leaders through a transformative educational experience.

Job Description

Job Summary:

The Human Flourishing Program at Harvard's Institute for Quantitative Social Science (HFH) aims to study and promote human flourishing, and to develop systematic approaches to the synthesis of knowledge across disciplines.

As part of this mission, the Program has launched a series of initiatives focused on making impact and advancing human flourishing out into the world. The recently launched initiative, the Academic Flourishing Initiative (AFI), focuses on using the flourishing measure to assess if colleges and universities are achieving their vision and mission statements -- which typically aspire to transform students into intellectually capable and virtuous leaders of society. A number of member colleges and universities participate as members of the AFI data collaborative which is a major source of revenue for AFI. The first year included 19 institutions.

The Program Manager position is responsible for the oversight, development, and growth of the AFI Initiative. This position reports to the Associate Director for Research and works closely with the Executive Director and the Director of HFH. The Program Manager liaises with IQSS Business Operations team as needed on administrative, financial, and HR related activities. The position also engages with leaders of colleges and universities for recruitment, onboarding, and sharing of reports.

Job-Specific Responsibilities:

Develop the structure and strategy for AFI.

Working closely with Director, Executive Director, and Associate Director for Research, create strategy and five year plan.
Develop strategy to create optimal portfolio for types of institutions in addition to how to best communicate findings and advance flourishing in these institutions.

High-level recruitment
and engagement of current and prospect members of the AFI data collaborative, often at the president or provost level.

Lead recruitment efforts including discussions with leadership of prospect institutions.
Develop and execute engagement, communications and marketing plan.
Oversee high-level gatherings such as large group sessions with member institution leadership, recruitment events, and sessions to promote findings and opportunities.
Develop content and materials for these efforts.
Onboarding process for member institutions.
Development of Data Use Agreement with institutions and interface with Harvard OGC and OSP for that purpose.

AFI revenue strategy development and oversight.

Development and execution of revenue models and strategies for AFI.
Discussions with institutions regarding revenue opportunities.
Fundraising efforts with donors and prospects.
Management of invoices and payment systems with regards to member institutions. Includes engagement with both members and Harvard finance.
Serve as primary AFI administrative liaison for HFH with IQSS finance administrators with regards to revenue activity.

Research report development and engagement with institutions.

Development of reports and findings for individual institutions and across institutions.
Engagement with institution research teams.
Engagement with HFH researchers.
Engagement with academic humility and academic freedom activity.

Lead communications activities for AFI.

Develop key communications messages for AFI.
Website development and oversight.
Press engagement.
Development of AFI collateral.
Development of other AFI media including videos.
Work closely with HFH Communications Manager.

Management of AFI administrative processes.

Recruit, interview, hire, train, and supervise AFI staff, student workers, and temporary personnel; assign and review work; provide ongoing feedback and coaching; and conduct annual employee performance reviews.
Serve as primary administrative AFI liaison for HFH with IQSS Business Operations team, affiliated faculty and researchers, staff and visitors; resolve operational issues and escalate complex matters as needed.
Develop and maintain internal tracking systems to ensure AFI activities are implemented on time and within scope.

Financial oversight
and management of day-to-day financial operations for AFI including budgeting and developing and managing systems that track finances, invoicing systems, purchasing systems, and other financial processes.

Developing budget, financial systems, and processes.
Entering, tracking and reconciling invoices, reimbursements, purchasing card transactions, and vendor payments in Harvard financial systems.
Monitoring AFI budget and research funding in collaboration with the IQSS Finance teams.
Preparing regular financial reports.
Flagging variances, or potential overruns, and recommends adjustments as needed.
Ensuring compliance with Harvard, FAS, IQSS, and financial policies.

Working Conditions:

Work Setting: Office.
Travel Requirements: about 15%, local and/or national.
This is a hybrid position with an expectation of working on campus three days per week. Exact schedule will be determined in conjunction with your manager and may adjust based on operational and/or business needs.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree plus a minimum of 5 years of related experience, preferably in educational and/or social impact leadership.

Additional Qualifications and Skills:

3+ years of project and academic administration experience.
Master's and/or PhD in related field.

Additional Information

Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week
Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position
Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Education, Criminal
Other Information:

This is a one-year term appointment from the date of hire, with the possibility of extension.
All formal offers will be made by FAS Human Resources.
All applicants must submit a cover letter to be considered for this position.
IQSS sits in the Division of Social Science. At IQSS, respect and fairness, kindness and collegiality, and trust and transparency are among the values we espouse and promote in our workplace culture. We work hard to ensure a healthy, inclusive, and positive environment where everyone does their best work in support of Harvard’s mission.

Work Format Details

This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that some of the duties and responsibilities can be effectively performed at a non-Harvard location. The work schedule and location will be set by the department at its discretion and based upon operational needs. When not working at a Harvard or Harvard-designated location, employees in hybrid positions must work in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts. Additional details will be discussed during the interview process. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment.

Salary Grade and Ranges

This position is salary grade level 057. Please visit  Harvard's Salary Ranges  to view the corresponding salary range and related information.

Benefits

Harvard offers a comprehensive benefits package that is designed to support a healthy work-life balance and your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. Because here, you are what matters. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

Generous paid time off including parental leave
Medical, dental, and vision health insurance coverage starting on day one
Retirement plans with university contributions
Wellbeing and mental health resources
Support for families and caregivers
Professional development opportunities including tuition assistance and reimbursement
Commuter benefits, discounts and campus perks

Learn more about these and additional benefits on our Benefits & Wellbeing Page.

EEO/Non-Discrimination Commitment Statement

Harvard University is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination. We seek talent from all parts of society and the world, and we strive to ensure everyone at Harvard thrives. Our differences help our community advance Harvard's academic purposes.

Harvard has an equal employment opportunity policy that outlines our commitment to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, religion, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law or identified in the university's non-discrimination policy. Harvard's equal employment opportunity policy and non-discrimination policy help all community members participate fully in work and campus life free from harassment and discrimination.
